title: ML data splitting and evaluation metrics
description: Stratified versus Group versus TimeSeries splits, ROC-AUC versus PR-AUC on imbalanced datasets, calibration, Brier score, and log-loss.

questions.text: Why is PR-AUC (Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve) preferred over ROC-AUC when evaluating models on severe class imbalance (e.g. 0.1% fraud)?

options.text: ROC-AUC divides false positives by all true negatives; when negatives outnumber positives 1,000 to 1, thousands of false positives yield a tiny False Positive Rate, making ROC-AUC deceptively optimistic
PR-AUC can be computed without defining probability thresholds, whereas ROC-AUC cannot
ROC-AUC is valid only for linear models, while PR-AUC works for all models
Scikit-learn deprecates ROC-AUC on datasets with fewer than 10,000 positive samples

questions.explanation: ROC-AUC plots True Positive Rate vs False Positive Rate (FP / (FP + TN)). With huge TN counts (e.g. 999,000), even 5,000 false positives produces an FPR under 0.5%, yielding a stellar 0.98 ROC-AUC despite precision being abysmal (less than 15%). PR-AUC directly tracks Precision (TP / (TP + FP)) against Recall, immediately exposing precision collapse.

questions.text: You are building a model to predict clinical patient outcomes where each patient has between 3 and 15 hospital visit records. What cross-validation splitting strategy MUST be used?

options.text: Standard K-Fold cross-validation
Stratified K-Fold cross-validation
GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by patient ID
ShuffleSplit with random state

questions.explanation: If records from the same patient appear in both training and test folds, the model memorizes patient-specific idiosyncrasies (genetics, baseline vitals) rather than general disease indicators. GroupKFold ensures that all visits for any individual patient reside entirely in either the train fold or the validation fold.

questions.text: A binary classification model with high ROC-AUC (e.g., 0.95) is guaranteed to produce well-calibrated probabilities.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: ROC-AUC evaluates only ranking order: whether positive instances score higher than negative instances. If you scale all predicted probabilities by dividing by 10, the ranking and ROC-AUC remain identical (0.95), but the probabilities become severely miscalibrated. Calibration must be assessed separately with calibration curves or Brier score.

questions.text: What does a lower Brier score indicate about a probabilistic classification model?

options.text: The model has high variance and is overfitting
The model has superior probability calibration and accuracy (mean squared error between predicted probabilities and actual 0/1 outcomes)
The model is predicting only the majority class
The model's decision threshold is set too high

questions.explanation: The Brier score measures the mean squared difference between predicted probabilities p_i and actual binary outcomes y_i in {0, 1}: Brier = (1/N) sum (p_i - y_i)^2. A Brier score of 0 indicates perfect calibration and deterministic accuracy.

questions.text: When cross-validating a time series forecasting model, why is random K-Fold cross-validation invalid?

options.text: Random splitting trains on future data to predict past data (lookahead leakage), creating artificially inflated performance metrics
Time series data cannot be evaluated with Mean Absolute Error
K-Fold splits cannot handle datetime index types in Python
It requires 10 times more memory than rolling window validation

questions.explanation: Random K-Fold shuffles observations across time, allowing the model to train on day t+1 and test on day t. This lookahead leakage hides non-stationarity and autocorrelation, producing validation metrics that collapse in production. Use TimeSeriesSplit or rolling forward validation.

questions.text: If a classifier's decision threshold is raised from 0.5 to 0.8, what typically happens to Precision and Recall on the positive class?

options.text: Precision increases (or stays same) while Recall decreases
Precision decreases while Recall increases
Both Precision and Recall decrease
Both Precision and Recall increase

questions.explanation: Raising the threshold makes the classifier more conservative: fewer instances are predicted positive. False positives decrease, typically increasing Precision, but false negatives increase, reducing Recall.
